title: Kolkata Durga Puja Pandal Crush Kills at Least 17, Organisers Detained
excerpt: A rain-driven surge at the exit gate of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin pandal on Saturday evening killed at least 17 people and injured 25, with later reports putting the toll at 19; police detained organisers and ordered a forensic probe.
body:
• At least 17 people were killed and 25 injured in a crowd crush at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening; later reports by India Today and Hindustan Times put the toll at 19, with about 35 people taken to hospital.
  • Police said the crush began at the pandal's exit gate around 7:40 p.m. after rain set in and an announcement by organisers sent the crowd waiting outside surging forward.
  • West Bengal will pay Rs 25 lakh and provide a government job to each bereaved family and Rs 5 lakh to each injured person; the Centre adds Rs 2 lakh per deceased and Rs 50,000 per injured person from the Prime Minister's relief fund.
  • Families tracing relatives can call the West Bengal helpline 18003455678; the injured are being treated at Calcutta Medical College and Hospital.

At least 17 people, including a seven-year-old girl, were killed and 25 injured on Saturday evening in a crowd crush at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said. The dead included 13 women, according to NDTV. Later reporting by India Today and Hindustan Times put the death toll at 19, a reminder that casualty figures in the first hours of a mass-casualty event in India often move as hospitals reconcile their counts.

The crush occurred at about 7:40 p.m. at the Sarada Park pandal of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja, off Chittaranjan Avenue in the Girish Park police station area, as thousands of visitors moved through one of Kolkata's most crowded festival neighbourhoods. Six of the dead had been identified by late Saturday, Adhikari told reporters.

Rain, an Announcement and a Rush at the Exit Gate

Kolkata Police said the crush happened at the pandal's exit gate amid "heavy crowds of pandal hoppers amid rainfall." A senior police officer at the scene told AFP that an announcement caused commotion after rain began, and the crowd waiting outside began "pushing, pulling and rushing forward and fell on the ground, leading to the stampede." Adhikari said the announcement was made by the puja organisers and described the rush it triggered as the immediate cause of what he called a "painful incident."

https://x.com/News5PH/status/2111617255012200951

Eyewitnesses told news agency ANI that people fainted in the press of the crowd and were carried away on motorcycles before ambulances could reach them. "My three friends were all trapped underneath. There was no situation in which one could breathe," one eyewitness said. Residents broke through another section of the pandal to pull people out, according to eyewitness accounts reported by The Business Standard. Witnesses cited in Indian media pointed to narrow entry and exit passages and poor lighting around the pandal.

"The stampede in Kolkata is extremely distressing. My thoughts are with those who have lost their loved ones. May the injured recover at the earliest."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister of India, on X

Organisers Detained, Probe Ordered

Police closed the pandal to visitors and detained members of the organising committee and private security personnel for questioning. India Today reported that 12 people, including organisers and volunteers, were detained, and on Sunday the general secretary and other office-bearers of the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja committee resigned. Adhikari said a fact-finding team would establish what happened, a forensic examination would be conducted at the site, and CCTV footage was being examined. Union Home Minister Amit Shah cancelled his Sunday engagements in West Bengal and said he would visit the injured in hospital.

The injured were taken to Calcutta Medical College and Hospital, where Adhikari and the state health minister visited on Saturday night. One injured person was in critical condition, the chief minister said. Police, fire brigade and disaster management teams remained at the site through the night.

Compensation for Families

The West Bengal government announced Rs 25 lakh and a government job for a family member of each person killed, Rs 5 lakh for each injured person, and free medical treatment for the injured. Prime Minister Narendra Modi separately announced ex-gratia payments of Rs 2 lakh for the next of kin of each deceased person and Rs 50,000 for each injured person, according to Al Jazeera's reporting of the Prime Minister's Office announcement. The state helpline, 18003455678, is the contact point for families seeking information about relatives.

A Recurring Failure at India's Mass Gatherings

Deadly crowd crushes recur at India's religious festivals and mass events with a regularity that investigators attribute to narrow exits, unmanaged surges and weak coordination between organisers and police. Last year, a crush at the Kumbh Mela killed 30 people. In Bengaluru, 11 fans died during celebrations of the local cricket team's first Indian Premier League title. In Tamil Nadu, 36 people were killed at a campaign rally for an actor-turned-politician, and in 2024 a gathering in Uttar Pradesh's Hathras district killed 121 people, as Reuters and other outlets have documented across these incidents.

Durga Puja is Kolkata's largest public festival, drawing millions of visitors to thousands of temporary pandals over several nights, many of them in the dense lanes of north Kolkata where Chorbagan sits. For diaspora families with relatives pandal-hopping this week, the practical steps are direct: use the state helpline to trace anyone unaccounted for, and expect tighter barricading, closures and traffic diversions around major north Kolkata pandals for the remaining festival nights.

What Happens Next

The forensic examination and the fact-finding team's report will decide whether criminal charges follow the detentions, and whether the failures were the organisers', the security contractor's, or shared with the police who sanctioned the pandal's layout. Kolkata Police are expected to review crowd plans for the remaining Durga Puja nights across the city. The Videshi will update this story as the official toll and the investigation are confirmed.
